binders: There exists a real constant c.
Universally quantify over a finite type ι and a measurable space Ω.
Universally quantify over a measure μ on Ω equipped with the typeclass assertion that μ is a probability measure.
Universally quantify over a family X : ι → Ω → Real and coefficients a : ι → Real.
Take a witness hne that the universal finite set of indices is nonempty.
Universally quantify over a real threshold t.
hypotheses: The finite index type is nonempty.
For every i, X i is Borel-measurable.
For every i, X i is μ-integrable and ∫ X i dμ = 0.
For every i, LocalDef001 μ (X i) < ∞ in ENNReal.
The family X is mutually independent under μ.
conclusions: Let K = max_i (LocalDef001 μ (X i)).toReal, A₂² = ∑_i a_i², A∞ = max_i |a_i|, and S(ω) = ∑_i a_i X_i(ω). Then μ.real({ω | |S(ω)| ≥ t}) ≤ 2 exp(-c min(t²/(K² A₂²), t/(K A∞))).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef002 μ X s means: X is measurable; s ∈ ENNReal is neither 0 nor ∞; ω ↦ exp(|X(ω)|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable; and ∫ exp(|X|/s.toReal) dμ ≤ 2.
LocalDef001 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of the set of scales s for which LocalDef002 μ X s holds.
K is the nonempty finite maximum over i of the real conversions of LocalDef001 μ (X i).
A₂² is the finite sum ∑_i a_i².
A∞ is the nonempty finite maximum max_i |a_i|.
S is the finite weighted sum S = ∑_i a_i X_i.
The measured event is the inclusive two-sided tail event {|S| ≥ t}.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that every nonempty finite family of independent, measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables whose exponential-moment scales are finite satisfies a Bernstein-type two-sided tail inequality for every real choice of coefficients and every nonnegative threshold. The decay rate is the minimum of a quadratic term governed by the squared common maximal scale times the coefficient square sum and a linear term governed by the common maximal scale times the largest coefficient magnitude.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The constant c is chosen before all probability spaces, finite index types, random variables, coefficients, and thresholds, so it is uniform.
The index family must be finite and nonempty; the nonemptiness assumption is required specifically by both uses of Finset.sup'.
The random variables need not be identically distributed; only mutual independence, measurability, integrability, zero mean, and finite LocalDef001 are required.
There is no restriction on the real coefficients, including the possibility that all coefficients vanish.

There is no explicit hypothesis that K, A₂², or A∞ is positive. Real division is totalized in Lean, so any zero denominator yields a defined quotient rather than an undefined expression; this can make the exponential rate degenerate.
At t = 0 the inclusive event is the entire sample space because an absolute value is always nonnegative; the displayed formula remains defined.
Although admissible scales themselves must be nonzero and finite, their infimum LocalDef001 can in principle equal zero and need not be attained.
If the admissible-scale set is empty, complete-order infimum semantics determine LocalDef001; the explicit hypothesis LocalDef001 < ∞ is intended to exclude the resulting infinite-scale case.
ENNReal.toReal is applied only after the explicit finiteness hypothesis on each LocalDef001 value, avoiding the otherwise exceptional behavior at ∞.
The left side is Measure.real, namely conversion of the ENNReal measure of the event to Real; probability-measure finiteness ensures the intended probability interpretation.
The tail event uses ≥ rather than > and is two-sided because of the outer absolute value.
The scale definition uses the exact threshold 2 in the exponential-moment integral, and excludes both endpoint scales 0 and ∞.
ambiguities: The dossier gives the scale only under the anonymous name LocalDef001; calling it a sub-exponential or Orlicz-type norm is an interpretation of its displayed infimum definition, not an additional supplied identity.
No claim is supplied that the infimum defining LocalDef001 is attained or that it satisfies norm axioms.
ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun is interpreted from its supplied type and definition as mutual independence of the indexed functions under μ.
The proposition does not separately state measurability of the tail event, although measurability of each X i and finiteness of the sum support that interpretation.
The displayed target alone does not specify a preferred numerical value for the universal constant c.
